meta.title: The Class Shop Prices
meta.textType: functional: a price list with times and dates

paragraphs: Lily's class has a project for the school fair on Saturday. The students will run a small shop. They will sell five things. Teacher Kim says, "A shop is a business." Every group in the class has a job. Leo is the manager of the shop. "I will tell you what to do," he says. Lily's group will write the price list. "Shall we put the kites next to the pencils?" asks Mia. "Yes, good idea," says Leo.

Lily writes the prices on a big piece of paper. It has five lines. Each price is a number. The first lines say, "storybook, twenty baht; pencil, five baht; postcard, ten baht." The last lines say, "paper kite, fifteen baht; eraser, three baht." Leo finds a broken paper kite in the box. "I will repair it before the fair," he says. Teacher Kim says, "The prices are low." "Rich or poor, a kind friend is better than money," she says.

On Saturday morning, the shop opens at nine o'clock. The shop will close at twelve o'clock. A long line of students waits at the table. The first student buys an eraser, and the second student buys a postcard. Mia is the third student in the line. She buys a storybook and a pencil. "How much is the pencil?" she asks. "It is five baht," says Lily. Mia gives Lily thirty baht. Lily gives her five baht in change. "Thank you," says Mia.

At twelve o'clock, the table is empty. Lily, Leo, and Teacher Kim count the coins. Lily writes the number in her diary. "We will spend the money on new books for our class," says Teacher Kim. "And we will save a little for the next fair," says Leo. Teacher Kim smiles and says, "Our little business is a success." "Shall we make a shop again next year?" asks Lily. "Yes, we will!" says Leo.
